topics.label: Welcome and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and introduces the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of Innate Immune Recognition: PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the evolutionary requirements and fundamental mechanisms by which the innate immune system detects microbes and tissue damage using conserved molecular patterns and germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families, Signaling Pathways, and the Inflammasome
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the specialized functions, cellular locations, and downstream activation pathways of key pattern recognition systems, including Toll-like receptors, cytosolic sensors, and the inflammasome.

topics.label: Sentinel Cell Activation, Endothelial Signaling, and Leukocyte Recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how tissue sentinel cells detect infection and coordinate vascular adhesion cascades and chemokine gradients to guide circulating leukocytes into infected tissues.

topics.label: Lymphatic Drainage and Antigen Transport to Lymph Nodes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the lymphatic system maintains fluid balance and provides a pathway for activated dendritic cells to carry antigens to lymph nodes for adaptive immune priming.

topics.label: Systemic Hyperinflammation and Septic Shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the severe clinical consequences and mortality associated with uncontrolled, systemic activation of inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammatory Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the passive and active mechanisms that terminate inflammation, the cellular processes of tissue healing, and the chronic inflammatory states that arise when resolution fails.

topics.label: Conclusion and Next Lecture Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture and introduces the upcoming topic on the complement system.
